questions.problem: A triangle has sides $x$, $y$, and $z.$ The sides $x$ and $z$ have lengths $3$ and $4$, respectively. If the angle $Y$ between $x$ and $z$ has a measure of ${139}^{∘}$, what is the length of side $y?$ Round your answer to two decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
The following triangle illustrates the information given.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14269732/assets/7eaca5e621843857786ceda924f110804482d490c9dcd2615c6b3e50b89cde8e.png)

The Law of Cosines states that

$$
{y}^{2}={x}^{2}+{z}^{2}-2xz\operatorname{cos}⁡Y,
$$

Here, we have

$$
m∠Y={139}^{∘},\,x=3,\,z=4.
$$

Substituting the numbers into the formula gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & ={3}^{2}+{4}^{2}-2(3)(4)\operatorname{cos}⁡{139}^{∘} \\  & =9+16-24\operatorname{cos}⁡{139}^{∘} \\  & =25-24(-0.754\,70…) \\  & =25+18.113\,03 \\  & =43.113\,03\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $5$ decimal places. 

Taking the square root gives

$$
y=\sqrt{43.113\,03}=6.57
$$

rounded to two decimal places.

questions.worked_solution:
We use the Law of Cosines to solve for angle $M:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡M & =\frac{{n}^{2}+{l}^{2}-{m}^{2}}{2nl}.\end{aligned}
$$

 
Here, we have

$$
m=29,\,n=20,\,l=13.
$$

This gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡M & =\frac{{20}^{2}+{13}^{2}-{29}^{2}}{2(20)(13)} \\  & =\frac{400+169-841}{520} \\  & =\frac{-272}{520} \\  & =\frac{-34}{65}.\end{aligned}
$$

 
Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠M & =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(-\frac{34}{65}) \\  & ={121.54}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to two decimal places.

questions.problem:
A triangle has sides $x$, $y$, and $z.$ The sides $x$, $y$, and $z$ are of lengths  $8$, $15$, and $17$, respectively. In degrees, what is the measure of the angle $X$ between the sides $y$ and $z?$ Round your answer to the **nearest tenth of a degree**.

$m∠X≈$
{{field-1}} ${}^{∘}$
questions.worked_solution:
The following triangle illustrates the information given.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14269732/assets/db40512e5f82f1625602c6e8a350ebcf49c2d85596ae89e71b869a50f895315c.png)

We use the Law of Cosines to solve for angle $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡X & =\frac{{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}-{x}^{2}}{2yz}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Here, we have

$$
x=8,\,y=15,\,z=17.
$$

This gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡X & =\frac{{15}^{2}+{17}^{2}-{8}^{2}}{2(15)(17)} \\  & =\frac{225+289-64}{510} \\  & =\frac{450}{510} \\  & =\frac{15}{17}.\end{aligned}
$$

 
Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠X & =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{15}{17}) \\  & ≈{28.1}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest tenth.
